content.value_statement: Inactive subscribers can damage deliverability and increase complaint risk. This skill designs a measured win-back path with re-consent and final suppression rules.
actual_capabilities: Defines lapsed cohorts using explicit no-open and no-click windows.
Creates staged offer ladders with triggers, timing, escalation, and stop conditions.
Specifies the action that captures renewed subscriber consent.
Defines terminal outcomes for re-permissioned and unresponsive subscribers.
Produces handoff facts for consent, lifecycle, preference, and quality workflows.
limitations: Does not send campaigns or modify records in an email platform.
Does not replace legal review of consent and suppression requirements.
Does not design general welcome, cart, or post-purchase lifecycle flows.
Cannot measure cohort size or performance without user-provided engagement data.

use_cases.title: Recover a Lapsed Customer Cohort
use_cases.description: Create a limited win-back sequence that returns consenting customers to active nurture and suppresses nonresponders.

use_cases.title: Reduce Deliverability Risk
use_cases.description: Define a sunset process for inactive subscribers before complaint and engagement signals worsen.

use_cases.title: Plan a Re-Permission Sweep
use_cases.description: Specify consent actions, preference handoffs, and suppression outcomes for an aging contact database.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Lapsed Cohort
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a lapsed cohort for subscribers with no opens in [days] and no clicks in [days]. Exclude suppressed and hard-bounced contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Win-Back Ladder
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-step win-back ladder for [cohort] on [ESP]. Include timing, message intent, [incentive], exit conditions, and a final suppression window.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Re-Permission Sweep
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a re-permission program using this engagement summary: [data]. Label measured and estimated facts, define consent capture, and resolve every terminal state.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Reactivation Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this reactivation plan: [plan]. Identify enrollment, frequency, consent, and suppression gaps, then provide corrected rules and owner handoffs.

output_examples.input: Subscribers have not opened for 90 days or clicked for 180 days. A 15 percent discount is available.
output: Cohort: Include eligible subscribers meeting both inactivity thresholds. Exclude suppressed contacts and hard bounces.
Ladder: Send a recognition message, a conditional discount, and a final permission notice.
Terminal rule: Restore confirmed subscribers to active nurture. Suppress contacts with no response after the final window.

output_examples.input: Our inactive segment is growing, but we have no current export or incentive.
output_examples.output: Proceed with an estimated cohort and a non-incentive ladder. Request the export as an open item before enrollment or performance reporting.

output_examples.input: Review a four-message reactivation plan that has no explicit consent action.
output_examples.output: Add a clear click, preference update, or reply that records renewed consent. Cap total touches and suppress contacts who miss the response deadline.

best_practices: Use explicit inactivity windows and exclude suppressed or hard-bounced contacts before enrollment.
Label facts as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Require an affirmative permission action before returning a subscriber to active nurture.
anti_patterns: Do not loop the offer ladder or continue sending after the final deadline.
Do not treat an email open as renewed consent.
Do not invent cohort metrics when engagement exports are unavailable.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It designs the program, rules, and handoffs but does not connect to an email platform or send messages.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide inactivity windows, engagement exports, available incentives, current suppression rules, and the intended email profile.

faq.question: Can it work without an engagement export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design the ladder from stated assumptions, but cohort size and performance findings remain estimated.

faq.question: How does it handle consent?
faq.answer: It defines an affirmative re-permission action and hands the resulting facts to the consent system of record.

faq.question: Does it create general lifecycle campaigns?
faq.answer: No. Welcome, cart, browse, and post-purchase flows belong to a lifecycle sequence design workflow.

faq.question: When should inactive subscribers be suppressed?
faq.answer: Suppress them after the final reactivation step and a defined no-response window, subject to your legal and operational policies.
